title: C# Questions & Answers - Method Overriding
sourceFile: Method Overriding - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on method overriding in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to declare a base class method while performing overriding of base class methods?
questions.explanation: The base member that will be overridden is declared virtual (or abstract). The derived member uses override.

questions.question: The process of defining a method in a subclass having same name & type signature as a method in its superclass is known as?
questions.explanation: Method overriding is providing a new implementation of a virtual (or abstract) method in a derived class, with the same name and signature, using override. (Same name without virtual/override is method hiding.)

questions.question: Which of the given modifiers can be used to prevent Method overriding?
questions.explanation: When an instance method declaration includes the sealed modifier, the method is said to be sealed method. It means a derived class cannot override this method.

questions.question: Select the correct statement from the following?

options.text: Static methods can be a virtual method
Abstract methods can be a virtual method
When overriding a method, the names and type signatures of the override method must be the same as the virtual method that is being overridden
We can override virtual as well as nonvirtual methods

questions.explanation: An override must match the name, return type, and parameter list of the virtual/abstract method. Static methods cannot be virtual. Abstract methods are already implicitly virtual and cannot also be marked virtual. Non-virtual instance methods cannot be overridden (use new to hide them).

questions.question: Which of the following cannot be used to declare a class as a virtual?
questions.explanation: Fields cannot be virtual. Methods, properties, indexers, and events can be virtual/override. A class itself is not declared virtual.

questions.question: The modifier used to hide the base class methods is?
questions.explanation: Used in condition when we cannot use virtually to override a base class method. Hence, we use 'New' to hide the base class methods and redefine the method defined in the subclass.

questions.question: To override a method in the subclass, the base class method should be defined as?
questions.explanation: A method can be overridden if the member being overridden is virtual, abstract, or itself an override (unless it is sealed). So the base-of-this-class method may be marked virtual, abstract, or override.
